experiments.name: Millikelvin torsion-balance de Haas-van Alphen and Hall/SdH magnetotransport of HOPG graphite, 30 mK-3.8 K, up to 12 T
experiments.plain_name: Detect quantum oscillations in graphite's magnetism near absolute zero
experiments.description: Measure the de Haas-van Alphen effect of a 10 x 5.5 x 0.5 mm HOPG piece with a capacitive torsion-balance magnetometer, then Hall and Shubnikov-de Haas resistance on the same sample (six-terminal Hall bar, AC currents below 10 uA), in the mixing chamber of a low-vibration dilution refrigerator from 30 mK to 3.8 K in a superconducting magnet up to 12 T.

requirements.rationale: The lowest measurement temperature (30 mK, where all FFT and phase analyses were done) must be reachable at the sample.
requirements.document_title: Millikelvin de Haas-van Alphen and Magnetotransport studies of Graphite
requirements.quote: Measurements were carried out at temperatures in the range 30 mK to 3.8 K in the mixing chamber of a low-vibration dilution refrigerator.

requirements.rationale: Cyclotron masses come from the temperature dependence of the oscillation amplitude over 30 mK-3.8 K (data at 30, 485, 980 and 3830 mK).
requirements.document_title: Millikelvin de Haas-van Alphen and Magnetotransport studies of Graphite
requirements.quote: Measurements were carried out at temperatures in the range 30 mK to 3.8 K in the mixing chamber of a low-vibration dilution refrigerator.

requirements.rationale: The magnetization and transport sweeps extend to 12 T.
requirements.document_title: Millikelvin de Haas-van Alphen and Magnetotransport studies of Graphite
requirements.quote: we report a comprehensive study of the de Haas–van Alphen, Shubnikov–de Haas and Hall effects in a sample of highly orientated pyrolytic graphite, at temperatures in the range 30 mK to 4 K and magnetic fields up to 12 T.

requirements.rationale: Hall and SdH resistance were measured on the sample in six-terminal geometry, so wired sample contacts are needed (the torsion balance is also read out electrically as a capacitance).
requirements.document_title: Millikelvin de Haas-van Alphen and Magnetotransport studies of Graphite
requirements.quote: the Hall and SdH measurements were performed on the same sample, contacted using silver paint, in six-terminal Hall-bar geometry. Standard low-frequency AC techniques were used with currents below 10 µA.

requirements.rationale: Optional detail: the six-terminal Hall bar needs at least six sample leads.
requirements.document_title: Millikelvin de Haas-van Alphen and Magnetotransport studies of Graphite
requirements.quote: the Hall and SdH measurements were performed on the same sample, contacted using silver paint, in six-terminal Hall-bar geometry.

experiments.name: SQUID-amplified piezoresistive cantilever torque magnetometry (dHvA) of PdRhO2 at 700 mK up to 15 T in a dilution refrigerator
experiments.plain_name: Measure a tiny crystal's magnetic twist with a SQUID-read cantilever
experiments.description: Mount a 300 x 200 x 50 um PdRhO2 crystal on a PRC400 piezoresistive micro-cantilever on a rotator thermally anchored to the mixing chamber of an Oxford Instruments MX400 dilution refrigerator with a 15 + 2 T magnet; read the cantilever Wheatstone bridge with a two-stage dc-SQUID null detector and record de Haas-van Alphen torque at (700 +/- 20) mK during 30 mT/min down-sweeps from 15 T.

requirements.rationale: The reported dHvA torque data were taken at (700 +/- 20) mK.
requirements.document_title: Application of SQUIDs to low temperature and high magnetic field measurements - Ultra low noise torque magnetometry
requirements.quote: Its magnetic torque was measured at a temperature of (700 ± 20) mK in magnetic fields up to 15 T.

requirements.rationale: The field sweeps start at 15 T.
requirements.document_title: Application of SQUIDs to low temperature and high magnetic field measurements - Ultra low noise torque magnetometry
requirements.quote: Its magnetic torque was measured at a temperature of (700 ± 20) mK in magnetic fields up to 15 T. Data were taken during magnetic field down sweeps at a constant rate of 30 mT/min.

requirements.rationale: The torque sensor is a piezoresistive cantilever read as a resistance bridge, so electrical leads to the sample stage are required.
requirements.document_title: Application of SQUIDs to low temperature and high magnetic field measurements - Ultra low noise torque magnetometry
requirements.quote: Self sensitive PRC400 piezo-resistive micro-cantilevers were used as magnetic torque sensors, which were mounted on a silver holder on the rotator.

requirements.rationale: Optional: the documented down-sweep rate was 30 mT/min (= 0.5 mT/s).
requirements.document_title: Application of SQUIDs to low temperature and high magnetic field measurements - Ultra low noise torque magnetometry
requirements.quote: Data were taken during magnetic field down sweeps at a constant rate of 30 mT/min.

requirements.rationale: Optional: lower-temperature operation to about 200 mK is possible with reduced excitation.
requirements.document_title: Application of SQUIDs to low temperature and high magnetic field measurements - Ultra low noise torque magnetometry
requirements.quote: Measurements to about 200 mK are possible by reducing the excitation current to approximately 100 nA.

sources.citation: F. Arnold, M. Naumann, Th. Lühmann, A.P. Mackenzie, E. Hassinger, 'Application of SQUIDs to low temperature and high magnetic field measurements - Ultra low noise torque magnetometry', arXiv:1706.08350

experiments.name: Synchrotron/VUV-laser ARPES energy-resolution test on polycrystalline gold at 7 K in UHV below 1E-10 mbar
experiments.plain_name: Measure electron energies knocked out of a cold surface by light
experiments.description: Cool a sample on a six-axis open-cycle liquid-helium-flow cryomanipulator to 7 K in a UHV analysis chamber kept below 1E-10 mbar, illuminate it with 21.2 eV photons (synchrotron or VUV laser) and fit the gold Fermi edge measured by a DA30 analyzer to obtain the combined energy resolution (2.67 meV); quantum materials are then measured, e.g. at 25 K.

requirements.rationale: The gold Fermi-edge resolution test was performed at 7 K, the manipulator's lowest temperature.
requirements.document_title: High-resolution ARPES endstation for in-situ electronic structure investigations at SSRF
requirements.quote: To test the energy resolution, we measured polycrystalline gold at T = 7 K (Fig. 6a).

requirements.rationale: Photoelectron spectroscopy is done under UHV to avoid surface contamination and electron scattering.
requirements.document_title: High-resolution ARPES endstation for in-situ electronic structure investigations at SSRF
requirements.quote: To avoid surface contamination and the scattering of the emitted electrons, the system must be maintained in a UHV environment.

requirements.rationale: The analysis chamber is kept below 1E-10 mbar.
requirements.document_title: High-resolution ARPES endstation for in-situ electronic structure investigations at SSRF
requirements.quote: multiple pumps, including turbomolecular pumps, ion pumps, titanium sublimation pumps, and getter pumps, are typically used to keep the vacuum pressure below 1E-10 mbar.

requirements.rationale: Synchrotron or VUV-laser photons must reach the cold sample and photoelectrons must reach the analyzer.
requirements.document_title: High-resolution ARPES endstation for in-situ electronic structure investigations at SSRF
requirements.quote: The analysis chamber (lower chamber) of the ARPES system is connected to two symmetrical incident light sources (the synchrotron radiation and the VUV laser), which can be conveniently switched.

requirements.rationale: Optional: mu-metal shielding against the geomagnetic field protects low-energy photoelectron trajectories.
requirements.document_title: High-resolution ARPES endstation for in-situ electronic structure investigations at SSRF
requirements.quote: Furthermore, the analysis chamber has a double-deck μ-metal shield, which is contiguous with the μ-metal-shielded hemispherical electron energy analyzer to counteract the geomagnetic field.

requirements.rationale: Optional: the reported quantum-material spectrum was taken at 25 K.
requirements.document_title: High-resolution ARPES endstation for in-situ electronic structure investigations at SSRF
requirements.quote: ARPES spectral intensity plot along the Γ−Μ direction of undoped sample with a photon energy of 76 eV at BL03U at a temperature of 25 K.

experiments.name: Local and nonlocal quantum Hall transport of hBN/graphene Hall bars on YIG at 2.7 K and 9 K up to 12 T

experiments.description: Measure Rxx, Rxy and nonlocal resistance of top-gated hBN/graphene Hall bars on Y3Fe5O12 with 7 Hz lock-in amplifiers (50 nA at 2.7 K, 100 nA at 9 K) versus magnetic field 0-12 T, gate voltage and field angle (manual sample rotation).

requirements.document_title: Transition between canted antiferromagnetic and spin-polarized ferromagnetic quantum Hall states in graphene on a ferrimagnetic insulator
requirements.quote: Transport measurements are performed using lock-in amplifiers at low frequency (7 Hz) with an excitation current of 50 nA at 2.7 K and 100 nA at 9 K as a function of magnetic field (0-12 T), top-gate voltage and temperature (T > 2.5 K).

requirements.rationale: The quantum Hall CAF-to-F transition is driven with fields up to 12 T.
requirements.document_title: Transition between canted antiferromagnetic and spin-polarized ferromagnetic quantum Hall states in graphene on a ferrimagnetic insulator

requirements.rationale: Optional: the Hall bar has at least ten numbered contacts (plus a top gate).

requirements.rationale: Data are collected at about 100 K to limit radiation damage; the procedure caps the temperature at 130 K (155 K absolute).

experiments.description: Mount a sub-500 um thin crystal in the slot of a miniature capacitance dilatometer integrated into a Quantum Design PPMS and record the relative length change from 2 to 50 K (alpha(T) by 0.1 K interval differentiation) in zero field and in 9 T; the cell can be rotated in situ.
